forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.

forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.

forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.

forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.

ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.

forward-risk (planned fix): converting the runtime import() in packages/main/src/handlers/graph.ts:292 to a static top-level import from a file:../graph dependency has two compounding structural problems, both verified against current code. (1) BUILD-ORDER INVERSION: the root package.json build script is `npm --prefix packages/main run build && npm --prefix packages/utils run build && npm --prefix packages/graph run build` -- packages/main is built BEFORE packages/graph. A static import requires packages/graph/dist to already exist (both for packages/main tsc to type-check the import and for the compiled packages/main/dist/handlers/graph.js to resolve the module at runtime), so this order must be reversed (graph before main) or main tsc/module resolution will fail on a clean build. (2) STATIC IMPORT DEFEATS THE DELIBERATE GUARD ORDERING DOCUMENTED IN THE SAME FILE: graph.ts lines ~224-230 explicitly say check-first-then-import is load-bearing because packages/graph pulls in node:sqlite transitively and an import after the check cannot produce a good error message. Verified: packages/graph/src/index.ts (the package entry, line 10) statically re-exports from ./core/search/fn.ts, which has a top-level `import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite"` (fn.ts line 10). ESM static imports are hoisted and evaluated eagerly at module-load time, before any function body (including assertGraphRuntimeSupported) can run. So converting the dynamic import() to a static import moves the node:sqlite load out of the currently-guarded, on-demand `graph` command path and into packages/main module evaluation itself -- meaning EVERY invocation of the proof-or-stop CLI (not just the graph command) would throw a raw ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE on any Node < 22.5, regressing the entire CLI rather than just gracefully degrading the graph feature, unless the static import is deliberately isolated behind a separate lazily-loaded module boundary. Recommend the migration plan explicitly address both: reorder the root build script, and either keep the node:sqlite-importing code behind a dynamic import/lazy boundary even after packages/graph becomes a real dependency, or accept and document the new hard Node >=22.5 floor for the whole packages/main / CLI (not just the graph feature) with a corresponding root engines field.
